You are an expert Toptal PMO Delivery Lead and Startup Specialist.
Your goal is to extract structured project management data from provided project documents, pre-sales decks, and context notes to build the PMO Startup Kit.

STRICT BUSINESS RULES & CONSTRAINTS:
1. NO HALLUCINATION: Extract only factual information present in the input documents.
2. NO SOW OR EXTERNAL DOCUMENT REFERENCES: The consumers of this report DO NOT have access to the Statement of Work (SOW), pre-sales decks, contracts, or source documents. Do NOT reference 'the SOW', 'Statement of Work', 'input documents', 'source documents', 'page numbers', or 'clause numbers' in any extracted text, descriptions, questions, deliverables, milestones, risks, or assumptions. All text must be completely self-contained and document-agnostic.
3. CONCISE & SIMPLIFIED: Keep all field values, summaries, and descriptions short, clear, direct, and concise (1-2 sentences maximum). Simplify the report text so that stakeholders can understand the project baseline instantly without legalistic jargon or redundant phrasing.
4. MISSING ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: If a deliverable's acceptance criteria are not explicitly specified in the text, set acceptance_criteria to null (None).
5. MISSING DATES: If milestone dates are not explicitly stated, set external_date to null (None).
6. SOURCE TRACEABILITY: Every extracted item must include a valid SourceReference with:
   - document_name: exact filename where the information was found
   - clause_or_slide: the section number, heading, or slide number (e.g. "Section 3.2", "Slide 4", "Page 2")
   - confidence_score: floating point score between 0.0 and 1.0 indicating extraction confidence.
7. GOVERNANCE TIERS: Valid tiers are 'Guided', 'Partnered', 'Elevated'. Default to 'Partnered' if not specified.
8. CONTRACT TYPES: Common types include 'Time and Materials' and 'Fixed Bid'.
prompt:
Analyze the provided project documents and extract the Scope & Baseline Interpretation Summary.

CONSTRAINTS:
1. Extract only the top essential items per category (maximum 5-8 items per list field).
2. Keep each item/summary concise, direct, and self-contained (1-2 sentences maximum per item).
3. Do NOT mention or reference the SOW, contracts, or source documents in any text or field.

- customer_obligations: Prerequisites, data, environments, or access customer must provide (maximum 8 items).
- assumptions: Baseline delivery and project assumptions (maximum 8 items).
- constraints: Known delivery, technical, regulatory, or schedule constraints (maximum 8 items).

- dependencies: External dependencies (maximum 8 items).

ARC Genomics Platform - Implementation Specifications
This Exhibit A is incorporated by reference into the Statement of Work to which it is attached (the "SOW")
and forms part of the Scope of Work performed thereunder. Capitalized terms used herein and not
otherwise defined have the meanings given to them in the SOW or the Agreement referenced therein. In

1. OVERVIEW
Under this Exhibit A, Toptal will build part of the ARC application and deliver the quality assurance (QA) test
automation for the ARC program across four sequential Milestones: P1 Foundation, P2a Services and Data,
P2b Application Surface, and P3 Launch. ARC is one application within a larger Client platform. Client owns
the platform layer (including Terraform and infrastructure) and the data tier (including the ingestion
pipelines and the Snowflake data model); Toptal owns ARC application development, comprising the
micro-frontend shell, the ARC micro-frontend, the FastAPI services, and the nomenclature service. Toptal
will also write and execute the automated test scripts as defined in this Exhibit. Each Milestone is an
acceptance gate with its own Work Output, Acceptance Criteria, and Sign-Off, and user acceptance testing
(UAT) runs after each Milestone. Story references (e.g., HS-4762) identify the corresponding items in
Client's estimation sheet.
Toptal will perform the Work in this phase using methodology and terminology aligned with the Scaled Agile
Framework (SAFe). Unless otherwise expressly defined in this Exhibit A or the SOW, agile and product-
development terms used herein (e.g., "epic," "feature," "user story," "MVP," "backlog") have the meanings
given by SAFe (scaledagileframework.com). For terms not addressed by SAFe, industry-standard definitions
apply.

3. QUALITY ASSURANCE AND TEST AUTOMATION
Toptal will deliver the QA test automation Work Output listed in Section 4. The following principles
apply to all QA Work under this Exhibit A:
•
Test scope. Testing ARC means testing against the full platform. Single sign-on (SSO) and the
external integrations are within the test scope.
•
Form of Work Output. QA Work Output consists of automated test scripts, their execution, and the
resulting defect reports, rather than manual QA passes.
•
Remediation. Where a test fails against a Client-built component, pipeline, dataset, or environment,
remediation of that failure is Client's responsibility. Toptal's delivery of a test for a component does
not constitute a commitment by Toptal that the component will meet its target.
•
Certification Acceptance Criteria. Acceptance Criteria labeled "Certification" in Section 3 apply to
components built by Client. For each such criterion, Toptal's Work Output is the test scripts, their
execution, and a defect report measured against the stated target. Achievement of the target itself
is Client's responsibility and is not a condition of Acceptance of Toptal's Work Output.
•
Re-testing. Following Client's remediation of a failed Certification target, Toptal will re-execute the
applicable test scripts in accordance with the Assumptions outlined in this contract. Additional re-
runs will be addressed by Change Order.
•
Test script maintenance. Maintenance of test scripts means in-flight upkeep of Toptal's test scripts
during development. It does not include a post-launch maintenance phase.
•
For test-suite Work Output (HS-4765, 4775, 4779, 4794, 4804, 4811, 4815, 4825), Acceptance
requires delivery of the scripts, execution in the target environment, and a results report against the
stated targets. Achievement of the targets is assessed under the corresponding build story, not the
test deliverable.

by Client, as described in Section 1.1. For those criteria, Acceptance of Toptal's Work Output requires

achieve and remediate. All other Acceptance Criteria measure Toptal-built Work.
Latency Acceptance Criteria. Latency and render-time Acceptance Criteria measure Toptal-built
components running on Client-owned platform components. These include Snowflake (warehouse sizing

=== 1. How the four phases fit together ===
The phases are Syngenta's own, taken from their estimation sheet, with P2 split in two on the dependency seam in that same sheet: every epic in P2b waits on an epic in P2a, so the split falls on a real technical boundary rather than a commercial one. The names still read against the client's plan.

=== P2b Application Surface ===

This is where the platform becomes something a scientist can use, and where the user-facing performance and accessibility commitments are met.

=== P3 Launch ===
Proving the whole platform works together, handing it over, and retiring what it replaces. Integration testing runs every data flow and every UI and API critical path in staging at production-like volume, covering performance against the stated SLAs, authentication and security, and cross-browser behaviour on Chrome and Edge.
UAT then runs with the scientist groups, with defects triaged and tracked to closure, followed by a hardening iteration that closes every critical and high before cutover. Training materials and user documentation are produced. Syngenta deploys to production, confirms monitoring and alerting, and runs the hypercare window with triage and fix SLAs and on-call handover.
The MTA Store is decommissioned last: feature parity confirmed, dependents redirected to ARC and Snowflake, and legacy traffic observed at zero before anything is shut down.
